messages:
maria.g: hey team - trying to accept my GitHub org invite but it says the invite is for a different account. I already have a personal github.com account tied to my work email (ugh). anyone seen this before?
ashwin: welcome! yep this is a common one. did you click the invite link while signed into your personal account?
katie: pinging @ashwin and @devops-bot — maria, can you paste the exact error message (or a line from the invite email)?
maria.g: error in browser: 'This invitation was sent to maria@redwood.com, which is linked to a different GitHub account. To join the org, sign out of that account and accept the invitation from the invite link.'
onboarding-bot: Hi Maria — pls follow the onboarding checklist at https://redwood.dev/onboarding/github to speed this up :wave:
ashwin: easiest fix: sign out of github.com in your browser, open the invite email link, and sign in with your Redwood SSO account (use SSO / work email). If you don't see the invite link email let me know and I can resend.
maria.g: I don't see the SSO option when I try to sign in, it only shows my personal username + password. I don't have 2FA set up on the personal account (I plan to keep that separate).
julian: two options: (1) add your work email as a secondary email on your personal account and mark it as unverified -> this sometimes blocks invites, so instead remove work email from personal account and retry; (2) we can have an org admin change the invite email to your other address or reissue the invite after we unlink the personal account. Which do you prefer?
maria.g: I can remove the work email from the personal account. can someone resend the invite after that?
ashwin: yep, I can resend. quick steps for you: 1) sign into personal github.com > Settings > Emails > remove maria@redwood.com or change primary to personal email. 2) completely sign out and clear cookies (or use an incognito window). 3) open the invite link and sign in with SSO (or accept via the browser prompt).
maria.g: ok doing step 1 now. one question: will removing the email break any repos or PRs on my personal account?
julian: (typo) julian: it shouldn't — removing an email only affects notifications and login alias. your repos and PRs stay attached to the account username. but confirm your personal account still has at least one verified email before removing.
maria.g: removed the work email and accepted the invite! :tada: but I don't have access to the 'serving-runtime' repo yet — I requested to join the infra team in the invite flow.
ashwin: joining teams sometimes takes a minute. I can add you to the infra/team-devs (read/write) and docs (write) now. Give me a sec.
ashwin: FYI if you need to upload an SSH key: run `ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C "maria@redwood.com"` then paste ~/.ssh/id_ed25519.pub into github.com/settings/keys. This gets you CI access for dedicated infra.
ashwin: also, please enable 2FA on your Redwood account as part of onboarding: https://github.com/settings/security -> "Two-factor authentication". We require it for org membership.
julian: done — you should now be in infra/team-devs and have repo access to redwood/serving-runtime and redwood/console. Check again and report if anything missing.
maria.g: I can see the repos now and cloned locally. thank you all!! one last thing: I lost my recovery codes when setting up 2FA, is there a recommended place to stash them?
katie: store them in your company vault (1Password) under the personal > recovery codes section, and also keep a local encrypted copy if you're comfortable. security policy doc is at https://redwood.dev/security/2fa.
maria.g: added to 1Password, good to go. thanks everyone for the quick help :heart:
devops-bot: Reminder: Please complete the GitHub onboarding checklist so automated access audits pass.
